name: Hub'Eau Hydrométrie (France river levels and flow)
short: Live French river height and flow, about 5,000 stations; keyless.
summary: Hub'Eau is a French national open platform (publishers OFB, Vigicrues SCV and BRGM) that serves public water-information-system data by keyless REST APIs. Its Hydrométrie API gives river water height (H) and flow (Q) observations from about 5,000 stations of the French network, refreshed every 5 minutes from the PHyC platform with one month of history, plus daily and monthly mean flows over longer history.

tasks: stations and sites near a commune, department or bounding area
real-time water height (H) and flow (Q) at a station for the last month
daily and monthly mean flows with long history (from 1900 at some stations)
filter by time window and fields to limit the download

pricing.notes: Terms: use of the platform is free ("L'accès à la Plateforme et son utilisation sont gratuits"); the APIs are accessible without registration or prior authorisation.

latency.typical: About 5 minutes after upload; stations record every 5 to 60 minutes
latency.notes: Docs: observations are banked every 5 to 60 minutes in PHyC and the API is updated from PHyC every 5 minutes. Live check: the newest observation of station K437311001 was dated 2026-10-27T15:25:00Z in a query made after 15:40Z.

coverage.notes: About 5,000 hydrometric stations, run mainly by DREAL and other producers; elaborated daily flows for over 4,200. The pages read do not say which overseas territories are included.

licensing.summary: Terms of use: "La réutilisation des Jeux de données est régie par la licence ouverte Etalab ... Les Jeux de données sont donc librement et gratuitement utilisables et réutilisables, y compris dans un but commercial. L'utilisateur de ces données doit néanmoins veiller à citer l'auteur des Jeux de données." The data are raw, supplied as produced by the water-information-system contributors, who alone answer for them. The publisher may refuse access for abusive use. The terms do not mention AI training or resale by name.

human.unknown: Automated stations; no person confirms readings.

application.unknown: No signing or attestation is documented.

time.method: Each observation has date_obs in UTC (live sample: 2026-10-27T15:25:00Z).
time.unknown: Station clocks are not documented; timestamps are unsigned.

location.method: Station records carry latitude and longitude, returned on each observation.
location.unknown: Coordinates are the producer's own and unsigned.

content.method: Each observation carries a method label (e.g. Mesurée), a qualification label (live sample: Non qualifiée) and a status (live sample: Brute).
content.unknown: Real-time values are raw and unvalidated; the terms say the datasets are raw data and the contributors alone are responsible for them.

freshness.notes: Real-time observations kept for one month; elaborated daily and monthly means over long history.

delivery.basis: Docs: "L'API est mise à jour à partir de la plateforme PHyC toutes les 5 minutes"; stations bank readings every 5 to 60 minutes.

auth.how_to_get: No authentication or registration is needed.

endpoints.params: e.g. code_commune_station, size, format (json, geojson, csv, xml)
endpoints.notes: Station reference data. Sites at /referentiel/sites. Result depth capped at 20,000 records.

endpoints.params: code_entite (station code), grandeur_hydro (H or Q), date_debut_obs, date_fin_obs, sort, size (max 20000), cursor, fields
endpoints.notes: Real-time observations with cursor pagination. Live call returned date_obs, resultat_obs, libelle_methode_obs, libelle_qualification_obs, libelle_statut, latitude and longitude. Maximum URL length 2,083 characters.
Elaborated daily and monthly mean flows over the full history.

api.rate_limits: None published. The terms ask users to fetch only a subset of the data using the available filters and to prefer compression; abusive use can lead to refused access.
api.notes: Formats: JSON, GeoJSON, CSV, XML SANDRE Hydrométrie; CORS and JSONP are supported. In testing, a request to the older /api/v1/ path with a custom User-Agent got a 403 page while the documented /api/v2/ path with a browser-style User-Agent returned data; which factor caused the 403 was not isolated. The terms do not forbid automation and describe the platform as for those who "veulent automatiser leur téléchargement".
